scope: Complete supplied five-page main and two-page matched SI; nine figures and 33 bibliography entries. Cited full sources unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: Preparation of SnO2-Nanocrystal/Graphene-Nanosheets Composites and Their Lithium Storage Ability
bibliographic_scope.authors: Yueming Li; Xiaojun Lv; Jin Lu; Jinghong Li

interpretations.topic: Three charges create three named composites
interpretations.text: SnCl2·2H2O charges of 300, 600 and 1200 mg are paired with the same 100 mL aqueous GO input at 0.2 g/L. The products are SnO2/G-0.3, -0.6 and -1.2, respectively. All are stirred for 24 h at room temperature, collected, washed and dried at 100 °C. The GO preparation is cited rather than reproduced; this recipe starts from the supplied GO dispersion.

interpretations.topic: Coupled redox is the authors’ interpretation
interpretations.text: The authors interpret the process as Sn2+ oxidation coupled to GO deoxygenation, supported by SnO2 diffraction and changes in FTIR/XPS. The proposed transformation is not a balanced experimentally measured reaction equation. No unique oxygen content of GO or graphene, tin conversion yield or dissolved speciation is supplied.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Preparation and structural/spectroscopic discussion

interpretations.topic: Size and structure describe different quantities
interpretations.text: XRD gives tetragonal SnO2 and Scherrer domain sizes of 8.4, 7.8 and 8.4 nm for the three composites. The text’s less-than-10 nm TEM statement is scoped to SnO2/G-0.3. Figure 3 annotates d(110) = 0.34 nm in each sample panel. The predicted Bragg value 0.337 nm is reference interpretation, not a second measured lattice spacing. No unit-cell refinement or coordinates are supplied.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–3 and results

interpretations.topic: More tin changes loading and morphology
interpretations.text: TGA gives approximate SnO2 mass percentages of 63, 68 and 74%. The source attributes the slower increase in SnO2 fraction than tin charge to partial SnCl2 loss, without measuring a recovery balance. TEM indicates more oxide particles on smaller graphene sheets as tin charge increases; numerical sheet dimensions are unreported.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Morphology and TGA discussion

interpretations.text: GO bands are assigned at 1401, 1735, 1220, 1052, 827 and 1620 cm−1. The source assigns the composite-series 606 cm−1 band to Sn–O and interprets loss of several oxygen-group bands as reduction. GO Raman G and D positions are 1591.3 and 1365.6 cm−1; composite D/G ratios are 1.13, 1.25 and 1.34. These ratios are not particle sizes. XPS binding energies are scoped to GO or the SnO2/G-0.3 comparison as stated.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, FTIR, Raman and XPS discussion

interpretations.topic: Electrode processing is a separate supporting route
interpretations.text: Each composite is mixed with carbon black and PVDF at 80:15:5 by weight in NMP, doctor-bladed onto copper and vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 8 h. Cells use lithium foil, polypropylene separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC (1:1 by weight), with overnight soaking. These steps support the electrochemical measurements and do not demonstrate new nanoparticle structures.

At 200 mA/g between 0.01 and 1.5 V versus Li, reported reversible capacities are 541.3, 402.7 and 222.4 mAh/g. After 35 cycles, retentions are about 69.7, 34.2 and 33.6%; only the 0.3 specimen has a separately stated 35-cycle capacity, 377.3 mAh/g. The authors propose that larger graphene sheets and lower oxide coverage reduce pulverization and improve conduction. These mechanisms are interpretations, not directly measured stress or conductivity.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 7 and discussion

interpretations.topic: References and introductory values are not new product data
interpretations.text: The introductory 782 mAh/g theoretical SnO2 capacity, literature bare-SnO2 performance and prospective sensor uses are background. No standalone pure SnO2 comparator synthesis is given here. All 33 bibliography entries are retained, but their full sources are unreviewed.

analytical_contexts.preparation: Drop-cast sample dispersions on carbon-coated TEM grids and dry in air; grid metal and dilution unreported.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Raman discussion and Figure 4

analytical_contexts.instrument: Land battery testing unit, Wuhan, China
analytical_contexts.conditions: 200 mA/g, 0.01–1.5 V versus Li, room temperature; overnight cell soaking.

source_conflicts: Main p. 2 cites Figure 2a/2b for the 0.3 specimen TEM discussion; the 0.34 nm annotations themselves appear in Figure 3a–c. Figure locators and sample assignments are kept distinct.
Main p. 2 refers to Figure 6 for the Sn 3d doublet, while the actual doublet appears in Figure 5B; Figure 6 is TGA.
Figure 3d labels the horizontal axis Wavelength (cm−1). Printed axis text is retained; wavenumber-valued FTIR positions are reported without altering the source image.
Main uses both graphite oxide and graphene oxide (GO); source wording is retained without assigning a unique oxygen stoichiometry or treating them as distinct measured batches.

The source prose calls the 0.3 sample size less than 10 nm; the three XRD domain sizes and Figure 3 fringe labels are separately sample-resolved. The size bound is not copied to the other two samples.
limitations: Complete supplied main (5 pages) and matched SI (2 pages) author-read; cited full papers unreviewed.
Independent source audit passed; presentation remains pending.
Upstream graphene-oxide preparation is cited to references 24 and 25, not reproduced. Scope begins with the reported aqueous GO input; no upstream synthesis is invented.

Reagent purity/supplier, mixing order/rate, vessel geometry, centrifugation settings, wash repetitions/volumes and drying duration/atmosphere are unreported. Room temperature is not converted into an invented numerical set point.

Electrode loading, area, coating thickness, electrolyte volume, cell geometry and separator dimensions are unreported. No new nanoparticle synthesis or measured electrode structure is inferred from cell processing.
Scherrer domain sizes, TEM dimensions, spectral features, TGA composition and cell capacities retain their separate methods and sample scopes.
No atomic coordinates, refined lattice constants or molecular conformation measurements supplied. Identity cards and morphology/reference-cell presentation remain pending.
